Lia has held several roles of advancing responsibility within KPMG, spending the first half of her career serving clients as an Advisory consultant. volunteering.description: Bernie’s Book Bank collects, processes and distributes children’s books to significantly increase book ownership among at-risk infants, toddlers and school-age children throughout Chicagoland.  Bernie's Book Bank model recognizes that reading is the single most important skill a child needs to learn and provides the logistical bridge between where books are today, and are no longer being used, to where they are not, but are desperately needed.

KPMG believes strongly in supporting children at every stage of their academic career through our corporate citizenship programs.  We know that strong reading skills are the basis for future success, and understand that one of the toughest roadblocks to early childhood literacy in low-income communities is a lack of books.  We founded KPMG's Family for Literacy (KFFL) with the mission to improve childhood literacy by providing quality books directly into the hands of youth in the communities in which we live and work.

publications.title: A mobile two-way wireless covert timing channel suitable for peer-to-peer malware
publications.description: A wireless covert timing channel (WCTC) is an established method of concealing information within a wireless medium for the purpose of covert communications. The pervasive use of mobile devices motivates our exploration into the potential of a two-way WCTC suitable for peer-to-peer (P2P) malware, in order to raise early awareness to the threat. In this work, we demonstrate the efficacy of a two-way WCTC over local networks, the public Internet, and cellular networks. Such network scalability in a mobile-to-mobile WCTC would make the notoriously hard-to-defeat P2P command-and-control (C&C) structure a viable option for currently prevalent families of mobile banking and ransomware Trojans. Specifically, we developed an Android application with the capability to communicate with other instances of the application over local networks, the Internet, and mobile networks via a WCTC. We demonstrate the feasibility of this application through experiments that test its accuracy, speed, and overall effectiveness. The main concern is that our endpoint applications could easily be replaced with malware and P2P C&Cs. The likely result is that very-difficult-to-detect malicious network traffic would emerge, especially since popular intrusion detection systems, like Snort and FireEye, have no inherent mechanisms to detect WCTCs.

publications.title: A Partial Replication with a Sample Size of One: A Smoke Test for Empirical Software Engineering
publications.description: Performing a full external replication can be a hugely expensive undertaking. The aim of this study was to determine what could be reliably established by performing a partial replication with a single competent developer making good use of available tools. The developer was not constrained by artificial time limits and was directed to make good use of the Jumble tool for automated mutation testing and the Model Unit framework for automated state-based testing. The Java-based software under test (SUT) was Cruise Control, a car simulation system. The patterns of mutation kills and reasons for missed kills are compared with the patterns and reasons reported in the original experimental study which involved four groups of students who manually generated test cases. We conclude that it can be meaningful to have a single competent developer perform a partial replication as long as a checking team checks and, where necessary, revises the work of the developer. The approach can be viewed as a smoke test for empirical software engineering.

headline: Director and Business Advisor, Deal Advisory – Accounting Advisory Services
about:
I am a business advisor and member of the Accounting Advisory Services group within the Deal Advisory practice of KPMG LLP, a leading global public accounting and professional services firm. Throughout my career, I have provided business, accounting, and financial reporting advisory services to business leaders to help them successfully navigate the inherent risks, uncertainty, and time constraints associated with structuring and executing complex financial transactions. Specifically, I have worked with the senior executives of private and large, public multinational companies in both a pre-and post-transaction technical advisor role for financial transactions such as: an initial public offering of equity securities, a public offering or private placement of debt securities, business combinations, restructurings, and divestitures (asset disposals or equity separations), principally with public companies registered with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).   

My approach focuses on assisting these leaders not only with identifying transaction risks and challenging assumptions, but also on how to make sure that the complex and sophisticated financial structures employed by such transactions comply with financial accounting standards and regulatory reporting rules. 

I have earned the Certified Public Accountant (CPA) and Certified Fraud Examiner (CFE) professional designations and hold a Bachelor of Science in Accountancy from the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign. In the State of Illinois, I am licensed to practice as a public accountant before the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).

about:
With over 20 years IT experience, Erik is a Manager in KPMG's Federal Cyber Security practice where he guides clients through successful Zero Trust and Cybersecurity implementations. A Network Engineering SMP, he also supports commercial and government clients with Network and Infrastructure transformations. His specialties include Zero Trust and Micro-segmentation implementations, large-scale infrastructure transformations, IT Project Management and commercial M&A support. He was helped corporations and both Federal and State/Local government entities, including large branches of the US Federal government, City and County IT organizations, a global hospitality chain, major financial and healthcare institutions, and an internationally renowned live entertainment company, develop and execute strategies to reach their technology goals and realize greater value from their IT organizations.

Prior to joining KPMG, Erik was responsible for leading Colliers International's North American IT integration activities. In that role, Erik lead the IT discovery/documentation of acquisitions, architected IT infrastructure integrations, provisioned and migrated acquisitions to the Colliers standard technology platform, and lead the transition of post-integration support to the operations team. Additionally, Erik was responsible for leading or managing the technical portions of all Colliers North American Office Moves, Network Upgrades and Wireless/Networking projects. He also acted as project manager for multiple Unified Communications/IP Telephony projects.

In his spare time, Erik enjoys producing Festivals and Events, managing IT, A/V, Production and/or Beverage Operations.

Erik has served on a variety of boards and is an active volunteer with several arts and education non-profits, including the South Street Seaport Museum, the New York Public Library, and the Center for Wooden Boats. Prior to relocation to NYC, Erik was the senior board-member for the nation's largest young professionals arts organization--the Seattle Opera's BRAVO! Club--and part of Seattle Opera's Technology Advisory Committee.

A graduate of Seattle University, Erik has held a variety of positions in the US Coast Guard Auxiliary, including Financial Officer. He holds an active security clearance, and served in the USCG District 13 Honor Guard and has received extensive FEMA Incident Management and Disaster Response training. Erik has received several awards recognizing his commitment to Homeland Security.

headline: Economic Valuation Services Associate at KPMG
about:
As an Associate in KPMG’s Economic Valuation Services group, I specialize in providing comprehensive valuation analyses for clients across a wide range of industries and business stages. My experience spans recurring fund valuations, 409A equity valuations, pricing analyses, audit valuation reviews, M&A purchase price allocations, and the valuation of intangible assets. I have supported clients in sectors such as pharmaceuticals, biotech, fintech, and private credit, ranging from institutional investors to high-growth startups.

I graduated Magna Cum Laude from Seton Hall University’s Stillman School of Business, majoring in Quantitative Economics and Mathematical Finance. At Seton Hall, I was a proud member of the Buccino Leadership Institute, the nation’s top-ranked leadership development program for five consecutive years, where I developed strong leadership, communication, and analytical skills.

I am passionate about leveraging data-driven insights to help clients navigate complex financial decisions and create value. I thrive in dynamic, collaborative environments and am committed to continuous learning and professional growth within the field of economic valuation and advisory.

headline: Finance Manager @ KPMG | Turning complex data into actionable insights
about:
As a Certified Public Accountant and Finance Manager at KPMG in Chicago, I specialize in transforming intricate financial data into strategic, actionable insights. Day-to-day, I navigate cross-functional analytics, budget forecasting, and performance management to deliver clarity in ambiguity for clients and leadership.

I’ve built my toolkit around:

•  Data-Driven Decision Making: I dissect complex financial models, highlight what matters, and convert numbers into narratives that empower stakeholders.

•  Cross-Business Collaboration: Working across business units and functional silos forces you to ask the tough, clarifying questions. I do that regularly because ambiguity kills value.

•  Analytical Rigor and Strategic Thinking: My CPA background drives me to go beyond accuracy. I challenge assumptions, expose blind spots, and advocate for smarter outcomes.

•  KPMG Leverage: I use the infrastructure, insights, and global vantage of a Big 4 firm, but I am not a checkbox-driven bean counter. I aim to shape the conversation, not just feed it.

volunteering.description:
The mission of Willow House is to develop and provide supportive services for children, teens, families, schools and communities who are coping with grief and the death of a loved one. 

​Willow House is a non-profit organization dedicated to the needs of grieving children and their families. We are recognized as a leader in the field of children’s grief locally and nationally. Peer support group services are provided in four locations, Arlington Heights, Chicago, Libertyville and Bannockburn, including a group for children and families grieving a suicide death and a unique expressive arts group.

​Since 1998, Willow House has been the 'go-to' program in the greater Chicago area, called upon to help young grieving families, school communities and others in crisis as they cope with death. In 2001, the FBI requested that Willow House provide support to Chicago area families grieving the death of a loved one killed on September 11th.

Willow House has provided direct services to hundreds of families each year. Thousands more have been served by school and community outreach programs that span the entire Chicago region, from the far south suburbs of Chicago to the Wisconsin border and beyond.

Through donations, volunteers, as well as corporate and foundation support, Willow House services are provided at no cost to families.

My experiences during my undergraduate career all have aided towards my passion for accounting and analytics and have given me a strong and profound background to continue my growth in these fields. Through my involvement with the IU Men’s rugby club, Kelley-To-Kelley mentoring, my classes at IU and more, I have learned about myself that I have a passion of a working in a team-environment, competing, and acquiring new knowledge from opportunities that present themselves.

headline: Tax Associate | Corporate & Partnership Tax | Federal & State Compliance | Accounting & Financial Reporting | Aspiring CPA
about:
I am a dedicated tax professional passionate about transforming complex financial data into clarity, accuracy, and actionable structure. From preparing multi-state corporate and partnership returns to guiding low-income families through individual filings, and streamlining accounting records during month-end close, I approach every task with the same commitment: delivering reliable, high-quality work that empowers clients and organizations to move forward with confidence.

My experience spans the full tax cycle: developing state workpapers, preparing estimated payments and extensions, preparing and reviewing Schedule K-1s, and navigating the nuances of federal and state regulations. I’ve supported busy engagement teams by stepping into senior-level tasks, coordinating client deliverables, and keeping projects moving steadily toward their deadline. I’m comfortable owning responsibilities, communicating clearly, and stepping up when the team needs it most.

Before entering tax, I built a strong accounting foundation in journal entries, reconciliations, AP/AR management, and QuickBooks maintenance. Those early experiences sharpened my eye for detail and strengthened my approach to financial accuracy skills that play a big role in how I work today. I’ve also had the opportunity to support diverse communities, including Spanish-speaking taxpayers in my community, by breaking down complex tax concepts into clear, approachable guidance that feels both accessible and human. That ability to translate information, whether financial, regulatory, or procedural has become one of my core strengths.

What I bring to the table:
• Corporate & partnership tax return preparation
• Federal, state, and multi-jurisdictional compliance
• Schedule K-1 preparation and review
• Workpapers, extensions, and estimated payments
• Accounting foundations: GL, AP/AR, reconciliations, QuickBooks
• Client communication, issue resolution & cross-functional teamwork
• Process improvement, workflow accuracy & risk mitigation

At the core of my work is an unwavering commitment to accuracy, integrity, and service. I thrive in environments that challenge me to grow, solve complex problems, and collaborate with others, while continually deepening my technical expertise in tax and accounting.

experience.description:
Manager of Delta Cars LLC 

Delta Cars is a self started company that caters to customers that are looking to lease cars for a very affordable amount per month. The owner, Hari, started this business and quickly took me on as a "helper" of sorts. 
However, I quickly moved up the ranks and started managing individual jobs and was tasked to take care of major jobs around the warehouse. 
The owner also had to leave to go out of the country over the summer and handed all of his responsibilities down to me. This was a huge learning experience because I was immediately thrown into handling the entire company.

I was given complete control of the company and was told to keep it running smoothly as well as make improvements and upgrades wherever I deemed fit. 
After coming out of this summer, I feel as though I am very experienced in business and data management. 
I had to keep track of all the customer profiles and credit card information as well as what cars they had leased out and what insurance it was connected to. Additionally, each car had its own data sheet about past maintenances and upcoming fixes. 
Working as a manager for this company taught me how to manage my time and quickly adapt to new situations. We had to stay calm at all times in order to keep the customer happy and make them feel safe.

headline: Forensic Director at KPMG
about:
As a Director in the Chicago office of KPMG's Forensic practice, I support and navigate our clients across various industries through investigation, dispute, and compliance matters by both mitigating future dispute and compliance risks and consulting clients throughout the full dispute or litigation cycle. In the context of complex transactions, I work seamlessly with internal stakeholders, external counsel, and KPMG colleagues to proactively identify and remediate potential post-closing pitfalls and to provide first-hand insight and expertise into the post-closing purchase price adjustment process and neutral accountant arbitration proceedings.

headline: IT Support | End User Support | Frontend Developer | Passionate about delivering exceptional end-user experiences
topSkills: Cross-team Collaboration • Creative Problem Solving • Adaptability • Troubleshooting • End User Support
about:
Hi! I’m Juan, a versatile and adaptable IT support Analyst with over 15 years of experience, I am dedicated to delivering high-quality end-user support that elevate user experience and satisfaction. I have a strong background in providing end user support, resolving tickets, meeting service level agreements, and coordinating with Tier III teams and key stakeholders. I am motivated by delivering high-quality solutions that enhance user experience, satisfaction, and retention. I value collaboration, innovation, and diversity, and I enjoy working in a dynamic and complex environment that challenges me to learn new skills and technologies.

In my most recent role at UScellular, I consistently achieved #1 rankings for ticket resolution time and end user satisfaction, showcasing my commitment to excellence in user-facing technologies. I acquired a certificate of completion in Software Engineering from Coding Temple, where I learned HTML5, CSS, JavaScript, TypeScript, React, SQL, Flask, and Python. I also attended Columbia College Chicago and majored in Cinematography and Film/Video Production, where I developed my creative and artistic vision. I am eager to leverage my technical expertise and creative background to drive innovation in user-facing technologies.

Key Skills:

Technical Support: Proven track record in diagnosing and resolving hardware, software, and network issues promptly and effectively.

Problem-Solving: Strong analytical skills with a knack for identifying root causes and implementing effective solutions.

Collaboration: Thrives in collaborative environments, actively engaging with cross-functional stakeholders and subject matter experts to achieve project objectives.

Customer-Focused: Committed to delivering high-quality customer service and ensuring end-user satisfaction.

Adaptability: Quick learner with the ability to adapt to new technologies and methodologies, staying abreast of industry trends.

Communication: Clear and concise communicator, facilitating effective communication between technical and nontechnical stakeholders.

Languages: JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, HTML5, CSS3

Frameworks/Libraries: Flask, React.js, Node.js, Bootstrap, Material UI, Tailwind CSS

Databases: SQL, NoSQL, PostgreSQL

Tools/DevOps: Google Firebase, Google Drive, Visual Studio Code, GitHub, DBeaver, ElephantSQL, Insomnia, Postman, RESTful APIs, JSON, Jinja2, AJAX, SQLAlchemy, Webpack, Vite

experience.position: Deskside Services Advisor II / Sr. Analyst II
experience.description:
Report to Deskside Support Services Manager and provide advanced IT support to end users.
• Support client service professionals at various levels within the firm, including Partners and other VIPs.
• IT support at Tier II, covering approximately 1,200 onsite users and over 3,000 remote users in the Chicago area, as
well as support for the 36,000 users across the country who visit the Chicago office.
• Perform troubleshooting/break-fix, configuration, distribution, and implementation of PC and Mac laptops/desktops.
• Deliver high-quality second-level service and manage the technology environment, including ticket management,
asset management, and desktop service.
• Communicate proactively with end users from analysis through resolution, keeping them informed of status and
providing follow-up upon resolution to ensure customer satisfaction.
• Follow compliance processes related to the preservation of chain of custody and tracking of designated hardware or
components.
• Serve as a senior team member/escalation point and may be conferred with as a subject matter expert by other IT
personnel.
• Collaborate with IT teams to streamline processes and improve overall user experience.
• Ensure timely escalation of end user issues by assigning appropriate priority levels, escalating as necessary to
management contacts, owning the issue through resolution.
• Participate in the implementation of firm-wide IT projects, IT processes development, and documentation efforts.
• Apply a working knowledge of internal client-specific applications to troubleshoot issues, test and deliver patches,
product releases, and other firm-supported upgrades and enhancements.

• Developed MyPDP, an Al-powered application designed to generate personalized career learning plans, enhancing career progression for users by tailoring professional development paths to their individual goals and constraints.
• Engineered a user-centric survey flow that collects data on career aspirations, available time and financial resources, existing knowledge, and target expertise levels, utilizing React and TypeScript for a dynamic frontend.
• Collaborated closely with a cross-functional team, including a Product Manager, Designer, and other Developers, to ensure product alignment with user needs and market trends.
• Established a continuous integration/ continuous deployment (CI/CD) pipeline using
GitHub actions, significantly reducing deployment errors and streamlining updates.

headline: Making computers dream things that make people’s lives easier.
topSkills: Research and Development (R&D) • Creative Direction • Human Centered Design • Data Analysis • Applied Statistics/Mathematics
about:
I thrive in spaces where logic greets creativity, data tells fairytales, and tough problems go to take a vacation- as long as all that’s near a good coffee shop. 

I'm the scientist with the heart of an artist: a dreamer—of systems, ideas and connections that make tangible sense in the real world. Most of these dreams start as wacky ideas and end in direct and practical execution; and of course there's tons of bold questions that help to form unexpected answers. My work isn’t just about solving problems—it’s about rethinking how we approach them in the first place- then working on getting them right in your hands. 

What I’m good at:

	•	Transforming abstract complexity into clear, actionable solutions and insights. 
	•	Making data less of a spreadsheet, and more like a story. 
	•	Bulleted lists and breaking the fourth wall- if you're reading this, try it sometime; I promise you it's a fun time!
	•	Identifying technical requirements that align to a perspective of aspirational goals. 
	•	Building solutions that don’t "work" —they work for people, because they were designed to.
	•	Asking the questions no one else is asking and refusing to settle for easy answers. 

I bring my innovative mindset to life in my role at KPMG Ignition- where I currently lead our team to design and develop new and exciting products and experiences in the realm of data science, AI and emerging technology. It's a constant feed of new projects that come from a spectrum of industries- but the common thread between all of my work is that everything is centered from the human perspective- and is built to suit that. AI, data science, and analytics aren’t magic— they’re tools built by people attempting to teach computers how to behave like humans using a ton of math. My job is to help us understand how we can wield them thoughtfully, ethically, and in ways that amplify and augment the human experience, making our lives easier- starting with the data we pull- the process built to interact, and the output that serves. 

Outside work- I'm a creative. Always listening to and producing music, or drawing and visualizing the things that pass through my mind.

So- after all that- I’d love to connect and talk about what’s going on with your journey with data and AI- especially if your’e into building things that push boundaries with a little bit of charismatic whimsy thrown in. There’s no challenge I’m afraid of.
